findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A repo uses `forge test --pytest` with `ruff check .; pytest tests` and changes a file with no related pytest tests.
`test_parts` returns no parts for the semicolon, but this condition no longer delegates that case to `close_tests`. With no picked or required tests, lines 831–834 return success without running Ruff or pytest. Previously, `close_tests` ran the unsupported shell command whole, so this can now produce a green result while skipping a failing check.
findings.title: Preserve unsupported shell commands when no tests match

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A repo configures `cd backend && pytest tests` and changes one backend test.
This routes the whole command through the picker, but its excluded paths are relative to the repository root. Pytest resolves those paths from `backend`, so `backend/tests/test_unrelated.py` points to the wrong file and the unrelated test still runs. The new case in `tests/test_affected_split.py:373-384` contains exactly this failing unrelated test. Required-test paths have the same working-directory mismatch. See [pytest's ignore-path handling](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/9.1.1/src/_pytest/main.py#L419-L430).
findings.title: Honor pytest's working directory when excluding files

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A new or upgraded repo has no `fast_test` and its worker runs bare `forge test` with `cd backend && pytest tests`, an environment assignment, or a single `pytest -k smoke` command.
The broader recognition is used only after entering the picker. `src/forge/review.py:370-372` still calls `test_parts` with its default plain mode to decide whether a worker should enter it; steps after `cd` and filtered calls are classified as non-Python. The worker therefore runs the whole configured pytest command instead of restoring the previous selection.
findings.title: Restore legacy selection for bare worker test runs

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A `package.json` test script runs pytest and the configured command is `npm test && node check.js`.
The single-recognized-runner path passes the whole chain to the picker. Since there is no literal `pytest` token in that chain, `narrow_command` at lines 138–140 appends the selection plugin options to `node check.js`, leaving npm's pytest run whole. A Python launcher followed by a check has the same problem. Forge's optional-package wrapper from `src/forge/init.py:75` instead receives those options after its closing parenthesis, causing a shell syntax error on POSIX.
findings.title: Forward picker options to the actual pytest launcher

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A repo runs `pytest tests/unit` and a change touches only `tests/integration/test_order.py`, with no required tests configured.
Using the repository root for every non-per-step selection marks the integration test as picked even though pytest cannot collect it. All unit files are then excluded at line 837, and pytest exits with no tests collected instead of skipping this step successfully. Before this change, `pytest_roots` constrained the selection to the configured unit directory.
findings.title: Keep a single pytest command within its configured paths

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - A worker uses bare `forge test` without a `fast_test` setting.
The new regression invokes only `forge test --pytest`; `tests/test_affected_split.py` exercises `--change`, and the bare-command case in `tests/test_worker_tests_stay_bounded.py` uses a plain pytest command. These tests can pass while bare worker runs with `cd`, environment setup, or `-k` still run the whole suite. This Done-when behavior needs a command-level test at the bare worker entry point.
findings.title: Gate: Bare forge test with setup or filtered pytest

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Gate
Case: normal use - A coordinator relies on the shipped guidance to determine which tests a change run will execute.
This change narrows a single pytest run after `cd` or with `-k` or `-m`, but `src/forge/templates/skill.md:1783-1785` and `:1849-1851` still say those calls run whole. The repository rule requires a change to what a coordinator or worker can use to update that template or the worker brief in the same change. The stale guidance can lead the coordinator to assume a wider test run occurred.
findings.title: Gate: Update the shipped pytest-selection guidance

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - The fix is checked against its promised Linux and Windows full runs.
The owner-approved Done-when is: “Every pytest command Forge narrowed before the chained-command change is narrowed again, and main's full run on Linux and Windows is green.” The supplied proof records only macOS local proof. The pull-request job in `.github/workflows/forge.yml:41-80` runs related Linux tests; its full suite runs only on schedule or dispatch. The Windows job in `.github/workflows/forge-next.yml:68-70,135` also runs only on schedule or dispatch and selects `-m platform`. This new setup-and-launcher test has no platform marker, so that Windows job would omit it. There is no supplied full-run result or pull-request check behind the promised cross-platform proof.
